rv.q: Somehow, the show never quite transcends its devices; it's just too familiar a scenario and you see what's coming down the pike before it actually arrives.
The experience here is noble, nostalgic, achingly personal and deserves all praise.

It was at that point that Ollie decided that it was time to pull the plug on the act. Now, with Ollie gone, Pompey has the blues, blaming his faulty memory for the demise of their successful career. Marsha, Pompey’s adult daughter, suddenly arrives at her father’s vermin-infested flat, rousing him from his reverie.
Smith's play truly compels audiences to engage deeply with the story, making Golden Leaf Ragtime Blues a charming and insightful work.
But the two lead performers are so strong that your cynicism will get the hook.
There are some predictable elements in the story, but the performances here make up for them.

I am not one to give away the ending to a play that has a unique and fulfilling ending, so I will only tell you that these two unique personalities, that have zero in common, end up doing the right thing in order for each to go forward with their individual lives.
